summary.title: BPF Performance Tools (book)
summary.one_liner: Brendan Gregg's 2019 book on using and writing BPF/eBPF tools (BCC and bpftrace) for Linux performance analysis, observability and troubleshooting.
keywords: how to trace linux kernel without overhead
takeaways: BPF (eBPF) is an in-kernel execution engine that lets safe custom programs extend kernel observability; BCC and bpftrace are the main front-ends.
The book covers over 150 BPF tools across CPUs, memory, disks, file systems, networking, languages, containers, hypervisors, security and the kernel.
Tools are usable as a ready-to-run reference or as a guide to developing new tools; no programming is required to use them.
Linux 4.9 or later is needed for the tools; BSD and other OSes are not covered in this edition.
Errata and updates list fixes for the 1st printing and bpftrace features added after publication; buy a later printing to get the fixes.
summary.summary: This is the official homepage for Brendan Gregg's book BPF Performance Tools (Addison Wesley, 2019). The page describes what BPF/eBPF is, shows example output from tools such as readahead.bt, tcplife and jnistacks.bt, and states the audience and Linux version requirements. It lists the book's chapter structure (technologies, CPUs, memory, file systems, disk I/O, networking, languages, containers and more) and appendices. It also includes an errata list, notes on updates to bpftrace and BCC, and a warning about pirated early drafts.
